description:
Somos Jp-ter; un equipo de cuatro personas: tres ingenieras en sistemas y un estudiante de informática. Esta es nuestra primera hackathon (nos motiva salir de nuestra zona de confort y probar cosas nuevas.)

Entre nosotros combinamos experiencia en desarrollo web, bases de datos y análisis de datos, buscamos personas con o sin experiencia que quieran integrarse a nuestro equipo
summary:
Rocky-Odyssey was developed as a web platform that identifies terrestrial environments similar to certain regions of the Moon and Mars. It takes into account temperature range and surface roughness and compares them with one another to determine the probability of a match.

We approached this challenge as a similarity ranking system. Rather than focusing on a single location, we compared multiple locations distributed across the world map to determine the likelihood of similarity. We sought to prioritize understudied sites such as the Gobi, the Danakil Depression, Tibet, Kamchatka, and Tibesti, while using some classic locations (Atacama, Antarctica, Iceland) as references. Finally, we normalized all the data and calculated a similarity score between each terrestrial site and each target.

The significance of Rocky-Odyssey lies in its ability to help researchers identify and prioritize unexplored regions that can serve as analog environments for the Moon and Mars. While the technology is currently being tested and refined in various well-known locations, the platform is expanding its capabilities to evaluate regions on a global scale, using methods similar to those applied to public data from NASA and other agencies.

Translated with DeepL.com (free version)
details:
What it does: It searches for terrestrial analogs of the Moon and Mars, prioritizing poorly studied locations. For 13 sites on Earth, it calculates a similarity score from 0 to 100 against 6 lunar and 5 Martian targets, using three variables measured identically across all three celestial bodies: terrain roughness (m), temperature range (K), and ice or snow coverage (0 to 100). The score is adjusted based on how well-researched each site is. [Describe what the interface displays.]

Impact: It helps select terrain for training, testing equipment, and planning missions, as well as discovering under-explored sites. Each data point has its source recorded (layer, URL, and date).

Tools: Python (pandas, numpy, rasterio), CSV and JSON, Git and GitHub. Data: MODIS and ASTER (Earth, 2023), LOLA and Diviner (Moon), MOLA and Mars Climate Database (Mars). [Add back-end and front-end.]

Creativity: Same definitions and units across all three celestial bodies, and a penalty that favors the unknown.

Factors considered: We document where the analogy breaks down (atmosphere, gravity, and radiation) and which values are approximate (5.5 km grid, Mars data from a climate model, coarse grid cells on the Moon).
